Meta's ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC. Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the company is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting users to organize their saved posts in Muse. About 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public. Many of those saved items, the person said, are either shoppable items or ads. A senior executive told CNBC that Muse, even without ads, "is still very valuable for our ads business because it raises conversions for advertisers." It does this by reducing friction in the shopping process and allowing users to go back to items later, said the executive, who asked not to be named because the details have not been reported publicly.

Erachin Daf 7 

The Daf discusses a Goses and a person being taken to execution. They have no practical Damim because nobody would pay for them on the slave market. A Goses is also not Ne’erach because he cannot be stood before the Kohen, while there is a Machlokes whether a condemned person can still have the Torah’s fixed Erech.

A condemned person is still alive and can make a Neder, an Erech pledge and be Makdish property. The Daf discusses what happens if he damages property or another person, and whether the resulting debt can later be collected from his heirs.

This leads to Milveh HaKesuvah BaTorah: when the Torah itself creates a monetary obligation, such as payment for damages, is it treated like a documented debt that can be collected from the heirs?

Although a condemned person is considered a “dead man walking” for certain Halachos, we avoid unnecessarily delaying his execution and causing additional suffering. If his Korban Chatas was already slaughtered, the blood can be sprinkled for him, but we do not begin a lengthy Korban process just to delay the execution.

A pregnant woman sentenced to death is generally not kept alive until she gives birth. However, once the baby has begun to separate during labour, it is treated as a separate entity and we wait for the birth.

Finally, a one-day-old baby can inherit property and then pass it to his own heirs, potentially changing which family receives it. An unborn child is different: in a natural death the baby generally dies before the mother and therefore does not inherit her property.

*Assemblyman Schnall Sponsors Bill to Allow Early Applications for Intermittent Family Leave Pay*

Legislation sponsored by Assemblyman Avi Schnall (D–30) would allow New Jersey workers taking paid family leave in separate intervals to apply for benefits in advance, helping families avoid weeks or months without income while their claims are processed. Workers who take their leave all at once can already begin an application ahead of time. But those taking days or weeks off in separate blocks, known as intermittent leave, must submit those days after taking them. A worker who takes Fridays off to bring a parent to medical appointments, for example, begins missing pay before the state can review the claim for those days. “Families can go weeks, and sometimes months, without the money they were counting on to cover the days they missed,” Schnall said. “The bills keep coming while the paperwork is being sorted out. If someone already knows when they’ll need time off, they should be able to get that paperwork started before they miss a day’s pay.” Under Schnall’s bill, A-5832, workers who know when their leave will begin could file a claim up to 12 weeks in advance, and the state would be required to begin reviewing it immediately. For valid claims received at least 30 days before leave begins, payment would be due when the leave starts. For valid claims received closer to the start date, payment would be due within 30 days of receipt. The measure would help workers planning time off to care for a loved one or bond with a new child receive benefits closer to when they need them. “This won’t solve every delay, because people can’t always predict when they’ll need to stop working,” Schnall said. “But when a family can plan ahead, the state should let them. Giving the department time to process a claim before leave begins is a practical way to help these benefits reach families when the paychecks stop.”

Erachin Daf 6 

Rebbi Meir and Rebbi Yehudah disagree about a Nochri in Erachin. Rebbi Meir holds he can be Ne’erach – the subject of an Erech – but cannot make the pledge. Rebbi Yehudah holds the reverse: he can make an Erech pledge but cannot himself be Ne’erach.

The Daf discusses accepting donations from non-Jews. During the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash their help was restricted because of concern for Rifyon Yadayim – that involvement could lead to interference or delays. Later in the building, certain smaller, non-identifiable donations could be accepted.

If Hashem’s Name is written on part of a donated beam or other object, only that section is cut off and placed in Genizah. The rest of the object may still be used.

The Daf then discusses money designated for Tzedakah. In certain circumstances it may be temporarily borrowed and later replaced. Tzedakah has the prohibition of Bal Te’acher, but it does not have the same Meilah restrictions as Hekdesh.

Once Tzedakah money reaches the Gabbai, its purpose generally cannot be changed. Rav Yannai, however, would borrow Tzedakah funds and repay them because his borrowing ultimately benefited the poor by encouraging people to give more.

Finally, a donation given for a specific Shul purpose should not simply be redirected. This is particularly important with an identifiable Nochri donor, who may object if his donation is used differently from what he intended.

Erachin Daf 4 

The Daf continues explaining why Mishnayos specifically mention Kohanim, Levi’im and Yisraelim. Those serving in the Beis HaMikdash interrupt their Avodah to hear Megillah. Kohanim eating Kodshim are also obligated in Bircas Hamazon and can join a Zimun with Yisraelim eating Chullin.

The Gemara returns to Erachin and asks why the Mishnah specifically includes Kohanim. Although Kohanim have different Halachos regarding Machatzis HaShekel and Pidyon HaBen, they are nevertheless fully included in Erachin.

A poor person unable to pay the full fixed Erech is assessed according to Heseg Yad. However, if someone simply says “Erech Stam Alai” without specifying a person, he pays three Shekalim – the lowest regular Erech on the Torah’s chart.

Erachin applies to a whole person, not individual limbs. However, if someone pledges the Erech of a life-essential organ such as his head or heart, it is considered as though he pledged the entire person. A dead person has no Erech.

A Tumtum or Androgynos can have Damim – an actual monetary value – but has no fixed Erech. The Torah requires a definite male or definite female for its fixed Erachin categories.

The word “Nefashos” teaches several inclusions: women can make Erachin, many people can be included in a pledge, and even someone with virtually no market value still receives the Torah’s full fixed Erech.

Daf 3 Erachin 3 

The Daf continues examining places where the Mishnah says “Hakol.” A child who reaches Chinuch is trained in Shofar, while women are obligated in Megillah because they were also included in the miracle of Purim.

Women can make a Zimun among themselves. The Daf also discusses a child joining Zimun once he understands to Whom we are bentching, as well as the wording women use in Bircas Hamazon regarding Bris.

Even very young children are included in several laws of Tumah. A one-day-old child can become Tamei through Zivah, and a Katan can contract Tumas Meis or have Tzaraas. Only a Kohen gives the final ruling on a Nega, although a knowledgeable Yisrael can guide him.

The Daf discusses who may prepare and sprinkle the Mei Chatas of the Parah Adumah, and “Hakol Shochtin,” including cases involving a Kusi and a Mumar LeTeiavon.

A person can insist on moving to Eretz Yisrael even from a nicer home to a worse one, and cannot be forced to leave. The same applies even more strongly to Yerushalayim – one can insist on moving there and cannot be forced to leave for a nicer home elsewhere.

Finally, the Daf explains why Kohanim are specifically included in Sukkah, Tzitzis, Tefillin and Shofar. Despite their special Avodah and Bigdei Kehunah, these regular Mitzvos still apply. Even the Kohen Gadol has space between the Tzitz and Mitznefes for his Tefillin Shel Rosh.

 בעל ה'בת עין', הטמון בבית החיים העתיק בצפת, נקרא על שם הספר שחיבר. מדובר באחד מספרי היסוד בתורת החסידות, והוא מלא עצות והדרכות מלהיבות בעבודת ה' לצד פירושים וחידושים מופלאים.

 סגולה נפלאה היא לערוך סעודה לרגל יום פטירתו של הצדיק. מובא כי העורך סעודה בתאריך זה זוכה לישועות גלויות ובפרט בזיווגים ובזרע של קיימא. (בהזדמנות זו נזכיר שה'בת עין' עצמו היה חשוך ילדים).

בספרו 'בת עין', מרבה הרב לדבר אודות ההכנעה וההתרחקות מכל שמץ של גאווה וגסות רוח. מסופר עליו שכאשר נפרד מבני קהילתו באירופה טרם עלותו על הספינה שהובילה אותו לארץ ישראל, התקשו בני הקהילה להיפרד. השיב להם בעל ה'בת עין': "חז"ל אמרו על הפסוק: 'ולדבקה בו', וכי אפשר לו לאדם להידבק בשכינה? אלא הידבק במידותיו מה הוא רחום וחנון וגומל חסדים, אף אתה רחום וחנון וגומל חסדים", ומכאן – שעל ידי שדבקים במידותיו של אדם נחשבים כדבוקים בו עצמו – אף אתם דבקו עצמכם במידותיי אשר הורגלתי בהם מנעוריי עד היום הזה, ותהיו כדבוקים בי ממש. המידות שהורגלתי להיזהר מנעורי הם – לשון הרע, שקר וגסות הרוח".

 בעל ה'בת עין' הרבה לומר כי על ידי ההכנעה זוכים להנהגה ניסית מן השמים. ידוע מעשה הנס ברעידת האדמה בצפת, בשנת תקצ"ז, כאשר המונים נקברו תחת המפולות, ורק עשירית מתושבי העיר נותרו בחיים. בעת שאירע הרעש, עמדו בבית מדרשו של בעל ה'בת עין' באמצע תפילת מנחה. מיד ציווה הרב שכל הנמצאים בבית המדרש יתאספו ויעמדו סביבו, כאשר הוא עצמו נשכב על הארץ בפישוט ידיים ורגליים לפעול את אשר פעל, ואכן, כמחצית מבית המדרש התמוטט ונפל הגג שמעליו, ואילו המחצית השנייה, ששם עמדו המתפללים תחת צלו של ה'בת עין' נשאר על תילו. המבקר בבית מדרשו של ה'בת עין' בצפת יכול לראות פלא זה. 

לאחר מעשה הנס, הסביר ה'בת עין' טעם השתטחותו על פני הארץ, כי ראה שאירע הדבר שלא בדרך הטבע – כי לא נפלו האבנים לארץ כדרכם , אלא נזרקו מדרום לצפון ומצפון לדרום, והבין שיד השטן בדבר – להחריב את עיר הקודש צפת, ובאופן כזה אין עצה מלבד ה'התבטלות', ולכן השתטח על הארץ ב'התבטלות גמורה', כדרך שנהג רבי אחא בר יעקב כשנלחם עם הס"מ, כשנתגלה לו בדמות נחש בעל שבעה ראשים, וערף את ז' ראשיו על ידי כריעות והשתטחויות. (כמבואר במסכת קידושין כט).

 בהתקפת הדרוזים על תושבי צפת בשנת ה'תקצ"ח חטפו אותו ואיימו לרצוח אותו אם לא ייתן להם כופר נפש, לאחר שביקש מים לשתייה וברך 'שהכל נהיה בדברו...' חלף במקום אדם בלתי מוכר וצעק על החוטפים כי אם יגעו לרעה ביהודי נכבד זה מרה תהיה אחריתם, לשמע דבריו נפל עליהם פחד גדול ושיחררו אותו.

כאשר פרצה בצפת מגיפה בשנת ה'תר"א, הודיע ה'בת עין' לתושבים המבוהלים כי לאחר פטירתו המגיפה תיפסק, ואכן כך היה. רבי אברהם דב השיב את נשמתו ליוצרה והוא היה קרבנה האחרון של המגיפה, שנעצרה מיידית. זכותו תגן עלינו.

For example, on a 10-kilometer stretch with a 90 km/h speed limit, drivers must take at least 6 minutes and 40 seconds to complete the section.

This means slowing down just before a camera will no longer be enough to avoid a ticket if the average speed exceeds the limit.

_Black Friday was named by traffic cops_
Black Friday was not named for retailers going "into the black." The name comes from Philadelphia police in the early 1960s, who used it for the terrible traffic jams on the day after Thanksgiving — officers worked 12-hour shifts managing the crowds. Merchants hated the negative name and tried to rebrand it "Big Friday" in 1961, but it didn't stick. The profit story only appeared in the 1980s.

United Torah Judaism is fuming over a draft outline presented by Gadi Eisenkot to MK Yaakov Asher, which includes a temporary deferral of service for young Chareidi men alongside high enlistment targets. Party officials said the plan was so absurd and insulting it was never even brought before the Gedolim.

In response, UTJ sent Eisenkot a public message, backing Likud MK Ofir Katz for Knesset Speaker and voting with the Likud in other Knesset votes on Wednesday, underscoring how the draft remains a major hurdle in Eisenkot's coalition efforts.

Naftali Bennett is advancing a three-step plan for a unity government with the Likud in which Gadi Eisenkot would serve first and Prime Minister Netanyahu second, Channel 12 News reported. The plan includes political pressure on the prime minister, talks on the draft and judicial issues, and keeping contacts with other parties alive.

But Eisenkot opposes any rotation in principle, and the Likud insists Prime Minister Netanyahu must head the next government. Bennett also said a government with the Arab parties has no public legitimacy and simply won't work.
